newsitem.title: CHINA: Yuan closes down against US dollar in Shanghai.
newsitem.headline: Yuan closes down against US dollar in Shanghai.

text.p: The Chinese yuan closed down at 8.3005 against the U.S. dollar on Tuesday in very dull trade and the exchange is expected to take measures to encourage trading, traders said.
The yuan opened slightly up at an intra-day high of 8.2995 from Monday's 8.2998 but fell to move around 8.3000 for most of the session, hitting a low of 8.3006 several minutes before the close.
Trading volume was very low, with most done at 8.3002, traders said.

"Trading was very dull because most traders had little interest to buy or sell with the price moving in such a narrow range," one dealer said. "The exchange is expected to take measures in order to make trading more active."
Dealers said that buying was less active than on Monday on concerns about selling by the People's Bank of China.
"Most people do not expect the yuan to stay above 8.3000 due to central bank intervention," said a second dealer. "So they sold and pushed the yuan below the 8.3000 level again."
Dealers expect the yuan to consolidate around 8.3000 on Wednesday.
The yuan closed slightly up at 7.4500 from 7.4600 against 100 Japanese yen and little changed at 1.0734 from 1.0735 against the Hong Kong dollar.
